manuscript_title: Effect of a Spaced-Repetition Mobile App on Grade 8 Algebra Achievement

manuscript_sections.name: abstract
manuscript_sections.text: Background: Algebra achievement in lower secondary school remains low. Objective: This study tested whether a spaced-repetition app improves Grade 8 algebra achievement. Methods: A quasi-experimental design was used with 96 students (48 treatment, 48 control) over eight weeks. Results: The treatment group improved by 25% more than the control group, t(94) = 4.12, p < .001, d = 0.84. Conclusion: The app is highly effective.

manuscript_sections.name: introduction
manuscript_sections.text:
Algebra is a gateway subject, yet many Grade 8 learners perform below proficiency. This study examines whether a spaced-repetition mobile app improves algebra achievement over twelve weeks of use in public schools.
The research question is whether the app improves achievement compared with standard homework. The hypothesis is that the treatment group will gain more than the control group.

manuscript_sections.name: methodology
manuscript_sections.text:
Participants. A total of 120 Grade 8 students took part, 70 in the treatment group and 40 in the control group. Mean age was 13.6 years. Sample size was based on a power analysis requiring at least 90 participants.
Instrument. A 50-item algebra test was administered before and after the intervention and scored out of 100 points. Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach's alpha = 1.12).
Procedure. The treatment group used the app for 15 minutes on four school days each week for eight weeks. 14 students withdrew from the treatment group, leaving 56; the control group had no attrition.

manuscript_sections.name: results
manuscript_sections.text:
Pretest means were 62.4 for the treatment group and 63.1 for the control group. At posttest, the treatment group averaged 68.0 and the control group 70.5. The treatment group therefore gained 9.4 points and the control group gained 2.1 points.
An independent-samples t-test showed a significant difference, t(148) = 1.20, p < .001, d = 0.08, a large effect. The sample was 55% female, 48% male, and 3% other. Table 3 reports these results; Table 2 is not included in this manuscript.

manuscript_sections.name: discussion
manuscript_sections.text:
The gain of the treatment group was 25% higher than that of the control group, which is 9.4 versus 2.1 points. The result was only marginally significant (p = .08), but the effect was large, and so the hypothesis was fully confirmed.
With 150 participants, the study was adequately powered. The twelve-week intervention length may have contributed to the effect.

manuscript_sections.name: conclusion
manuscript_sections.text: Among the 96 students studied, the control group declined, the treatment group improved, and the difference was not significant, which proves that the app works for all learners in all schools.
